newsitem.title: FRANCE: French GSM mobile phone market grew 9.5 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: French GSM mobile phone market grew 9.5 pct in June.

text.p: The French GSM mobile phone market, the biggest mobile communications segment in France, grew by 9.5 percent in June to total 3.39 million subscribers, ART, the French telecommunications regulator, said in a statement on Friday.
The figures confirm claims in July by the three main companies operating in the GSM market that June had been a record month for sales.

ART said that Itineris, the GSM service run by telecommunications operator France Telecom, drew 178,500 net new subscribers in June, a rise of 10.2 percent, taking its total to 1.93 million subscribers.
SFR, the GSM service run by Compagnie Generale des Eaux's Cegetel unit, saw a 7.7 percent rise in subscribers, or a net gain of 87,200, in June, bringing its total to 1.22 million, ART said.
Bouygues' Bouygues Telecom, the third GSM operator, launched in May 1996, added a net 25,300 subscribers in June, a rise of 14.9 percent, taking its total to 194,700 subscribers.

In May Bouygues Telecom added 22,300 subscribers, a rise of 15.2 percent, while France Telecom and SFR each grew their subscriber base by 6.5 percent, telecommunications watchdog ART said in a monthly report published on July 2.

The companies put the surge in mobile phone sales in June down to marketing campaigns where all three were running offers designed to attract the general public, the real attempt to win a mass consumer market in the French mobile phone business.

The country has relatively low market penetration, with some five percent of the population owning a mobile phone, a much lower figure than in Britain, or Scandinavia where market penetration is 25 and 30 percent respectively.
